verses.1: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to His disciples,
verses.2: saying, "The scribes and the Pharisees sit on Moses' seat.
verses.3: So practice and observe everything they tell you, but do not do as they do; for they say and do not do.
verses.4: They tie up heavy burdens, hard to bear, and lay them on people's shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to lift a finger to move them.
verses.5: All their works they do to be seen by others. They make their phylacteries wide and their tassels long,
verses.6: and they love the place of honor at feasts and the chief seats in the synagogues,
verses.7: and greetings in the marketplaces, and to be called Rabbi by others.
verses.8: But you are not to be called Rabbi, for you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers.
verses.9: And call no one your father on earth, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.
verses.10: Nor are you to be called instructors, for you have one Instructor, the Christ.
verses.11: The greatest among you shall be your servant.
verses.12: Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
verses.13: But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you shut the kingdom of heaven in people's faces. You yourselves do not enter, nor do you allow those who are entering to go in.
verses.14: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you devour widows' houses and for a pretense make long prayers. Therefore you will receive the greater condemnation.
verses.15: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you travel across sea and land to make a single convert, and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a child of hell as yourselves.
verses.16: Woe to you, blind guides, who say, 'Whoever swears by the temple, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the temple, he is bound by his oath.'
verses.17: You blind fools! For which is greater, the gold, or the temple that consecrated the gold?
verses.18: And you say, 'Whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift on it, he is bound by his oath.'
verses.19: You blind men! For which is greater, the gift, or the altar that consecrates the gift?
verses.20: So whoever swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it.
verses.21: And whoever swears by the temple swears by it and by Him who dwells in it.
verses.22: And whoever swears by heaven swears by the throne of God and by Him who sits on it.
verses.23: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you tithe mint and dill and cumin, and have neglected the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faithfulness. These you ought to have done, without neglecting the others.
verses.24: You blind guides, straining out a gnat and swallowing a camel!
verses.25: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside they are full of greed and self-indulgence.
verses.26: You blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and the dish, so that the outside may also become clean.
verses.27: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like whitewashed tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful, but within are full of dead people's bones and all uncleanness.
verses.28: So you also outwardly appear righteous to others, but within you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.
verses.29: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you build the tombs of the prophets and decorate the monuments of the righteous,
verses.30: and say, 'If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have taken part with them in shedding the blood of the prophets.'
verses.31: Thus you testify against yourselves that you are sons of those who murdered the prophets.
verses.32: Fill up, then, the measure of your fathers.
verses.33: You serpents, you brood of vipers, how are you to escape being sentenced to hell?
verses.34: Therefore I am sending you prophets and wise men and scribes. Some of them you will kill and crucify, and some you will flog in your synagogues and persecute from town to town,
verses.35: so that on you may come all the righteous blood shed on earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah the son of Barachiah, whom you murdered between the sanctuary and the altar.
verses.36: Truly I say to you, all these things will come upon this generation.
verses.37: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you! How often I have longed to gather your children together as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were not willing!
verses.38: Behold, your house is left to you desolate.
verses.39: For I say to you, you will not see Me again until you say, 'Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.'"
